articles.title: Google froze its open source bug bounty program due to a ‘significant rise’ in AI submissions
articles.full_text:
Blaming a “significant rise” in AI submissions, Google has paused its open source bug bounty program until next year.

Last year, TechCrunch reported that cybersecurity experts were warning of that AI slop posed a serious risk to bug bounty programs. Looks like that’s the issue confronting Google’s Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program, where researchers were rewarded for finding vulnerabilities in the company’s open source software.

In posts on X and the program website, Google said the bug bounty program was paused as of October 1, with a promise to provide “an update” in the first quarter of 2027. According to Tom’s Hardware, Google engineers and open source maintainers were overwhelmed by reports that were invalid or contained hallucinations.

“This pause is due to a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid,” the company said.

In the meantime, participants are encouraged to consider Google’s other bug bounty programs.
articles.summary:
Google has paused its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program after being overwhelmed by a surge of AI-generated bug reports, most of which were invalid or hallucinated. The company says the program will remain on hold until at least early 2027.

  • Core event: Google suspended its open source bug bounty program as of October 1, citing a "significant rise in automated submissions" that were largely not valid, with an update promised in the first quarter of 2027.
  • Background: The move follows earlier warnings from cybersecurity experts that AI slop posed a serious risk to bug bounty programs, as engineers and open source maintainers became overwhelmed by reports containing hallucinations.
  • Impact: The pause removes a key incentive for researchers to find vulnerabilities in Google's open source software, potentially slowing the discovery of legitimate security flaws.
  • Next steps: Google is directing participants to its other bug bounty programs while the open source initiative remains on hold.
